text:
mira: Quick pilot update: ran an opportunistic decode prioritization (ODP) pass during bring-up of draft-llama3-12b-quant across our small eval suite (dialog + summarization). ~2k prompts, mixed batch sizes.

ashok: TL;DR numbers? :eyes:

mira: p50 token latency down ~18% (42ms -> 34ms), p95 down ~12%. End-to-end throughput +22% on micro-batches (batch=4). Estimated per-token infra cost -15% on hosted traces.

lee: quality impact?

mira: small regressions on multi-sentence summarization: ROUGE-L delta -0.9, chrF -0.6. Hallucination-ish faults up ~3% on our longform set (mostly omitted facts or premature conclusion). Chat/dialog tasks unchanged for user-intent metrics.

sam: which quant & runtime config?

mira: tried three quant configs: int4-GPTQ, fp4, and int8. Best perf = int4; worst quality hit. fp4 is middle ground. Runtime snippet from the probe: 
```yaml
speculative:
  enabled: true
  loan_depth: 2   # how many speculative tokens we issue
  backoff_prob: 0.25  # chance to backoff to non-speculative path
  kv_prefetch: opportunistic
runtime:
  quant: int4-gptq
  batch_size: auto
  max_seq: 2048
```

linda: loan_depth 2 seems aggressive with int4. Did you try loan_depth=1?

mira: yes — lowering loan_depth to 1 and backoff_prob to 0.1 recovers most of the ROUGE loss (down only -0.2) and drops hallucination delta to +1%. Tradeoff: p50 latency uplift ~5% vs the aggressive config, but still net win vs no speculative.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary cluster x3 started (canary-id: c-20260318-odps)

ashok: we should not roll this wide until we have a controlled AB test. Plan: 5% traffic AA/B for 48h + evaluation harness of 10k held-out prompts (split by short/long context).

mira: agreed. I'll open the canary ticket with the exact traffic plan and attach the eval harness script. Also propose these targeted evals: 
- coherence over >800 token contexts (deterministic prompts)
- factual recall (QA set with known answers)
- repetition/hallucination counts (heuristic checks)
- response length distribution breakouts

lee: add monitoring hooks: tag logs with `spec_id`, `spec_config`, `quant_profile` and emit per-request decision traces so we can correlate quality regressions with particular speculative paths.

sam: on the AB metric side, what primary metric? Rouge? user clicks?

mira: for the internal evals: ROUGE-L + hallucination count + exact-match on QA. For production AB: latency p95 and downstream success (client-side accept/complete signal) as the tradeoff metric. We must set a rollback threshold: if QA exact-match drops >1.5% or hallucination +5% absolute, auto-fail.

linda: any quick mitigations if regressions show up in canary?

mira: yes: 
- immediate mitigation: drop to loan_depth=1 + backoff_prob=0.15 or fallback to fp4 profile for contexts >512 tokens.
- mid-term: retrain a tiny lightweight ranker to gate speculative outputs when quantization uncertainty is high (cheap check).

ashok: sounds good. Also run a focused ablation: speculative enabled vs speculative+kv_prefetch vs kv_prefetch only, across quant profiles. Need the matrix for our ops report.

mira: will run the matrix tomorrow and push results into the ops dashboard. Quick note: speculative decisions are cheap to log but will inflate observability volume; we'll sample 1% of requests for full traces and keep summaries otherwise.

sam: don't forget to include a deterministic seed run for the eval harness to ensure reproducibility.

mira: on it. Opening ticket now: https://redwood-internal/boards/edge/ODP-382 (will attach config and raw CSVs). TL;DR: ODP + int4 gives solid perf gains but induces small longform regressions; mitigations (shallower speculation, fp4 fallback) look promising. Next: AB canary + 10k-holdout eval + logging + rollback hooks. :thumbsup:
